cards.summary: 【TechCrunch】Journalists, entrepreneurs, and even some public relations professionals will tell you that the PR process is broken. But could AI actually make things better?

Journalists, entrepreneurs, and even some public relations professionals will tell you that the PR process is broken (buy me a drink sometime, and I’ll give you my rant). But could AI actually make things better?

Honeyjar, which will be attending this week’s TechCrunch Disrupt as part of the Startup Battlefield 200, wants to use AI to make the expertise and judgment of the best PR pros available to everyone, including founders who have no idea where to start.

The startup’s founders, CEO Michelle Masek and CCO Nadia Jamshidi, certainly fit the bill when it comes to PR expertise. They’ve both spent decades in the field, doing in-house communications and working at agencies. Masek recently served as senior vice president of marketing and communications for Ev Williams’ venture firm, Obvious Ventures.

As Masek described the challenges involved in “helping with the why and when of comms and marketing for 110 portfolio companies” (the startups her firm had invested in), I flashed back to my own brief stint leading marketing at an early-stage VC firm, where founders were constantly asking for help getting into TechCrunch. So I wasn’t surprised that Masek found herself asking, “Is there a way to scale the senior-level expertise into AI [in a way] that actually helps users do the work of comms in the proactive and skilled way that we do?”

Honeyjar is her answer to that question. It automates processes like writing announcements, finding the best journalists to pitch, and identifying the most promising speaking opportunities. But Jamshidi told me in a follow-up email that Honeyjar’s vision goes beyond getting press coverage and beyond specific AI tools.

“Honeyjar can find reporters, build media lists, scan news and social, track coverage, and surface opportunities,” she said. “Those capabilities are important, but they’re just one piece of what we’re building. The bigger idea is bringing the whole communications workflow together: signals, context, strategy, judgment, timing, and execution.”
And it’s not just for founders. Masek said she’s come to realize there are “millions and millions of unassigned communicators responsible for the work of comms.”

“They don’t have the title of comms, but they’re marketers, investors, authors, creators, school superintendents, sports team leaders,” she added. “It’s incredibly horizontal, this need to nail strategic communications. It’s always passed around, but the problems are very often not solved.”

Nor is Honeyjar trying to replace PR professionals. Masek said she and Jamshidi built the tool they wanted to use themselves. She argued that Honeyjar can make PR firms and in-house comms teams more effective, while allowing individual PR practitioners to “take on that third client without any scaling cost.”

When Honeyjar opened its waitlist, it received 10,000 signups in the first 24 hours, said Masek. Beta testers include Nextdoor, tech startup Coco Robotics, investor Bloomberg Beta, and agencies Mission North and Full Picture.

That sounds promising for companies looking to get more attention, but it could be a nightmare for journalists. We receive more pitches than we can respond to, many of them already written by AI chatbots.

When I raised my fears about getting inundated with even more PR slop, Masek noted that while Honeyjar can draft a pitch email or a social media post in the customer’s voice, the customer actually has to hit send or publish.
“We never want a world where the human is removed from the loop,” she said.

And that’s also where judgment is key. Masek said she and Jamshidi tried to “infuse and encode Honeyjar with our wisdom.” Through a broader initiative called the Comms Lab, they’re now training the product on the judgment of other PR pros as well.

“For us, judgment is knowing what to do, what not to do, when to act, and how to adapt to the situation,” Jamshidi added. “That comes from understanding a company’s goals and priorities, what’s happening inside and outside the organization, and knowing what to say, to whom, where, and when.”
In some cases, Masek said Honeyjar might even tell a founder that they’re simply not ready for coverage.

“We hear from reporters all the time who want better pitches, who want to hear from experts directly,” she said. “We actually see a future where there are more credible pitches in your inbox from sources who you actually want to hear from.”

记者、企业家，甚至一些公关专业人士都会告诉你，公关流程已经被破坏了（有时请我喝一杯，我会给你咆哮）。但人工智能真的能让事情变得更好吗？
Honeyjar 将作为 Startup Battlefield 200 的一部分参加本周的 TechCrunch Disrupt，它希望利用 AI 为每个人提供最好的公关专业人士的专业知识和判断力，包括那些不知道从哪里开始的创始人。
这家初创公司的创始人、首席执行官 Michelle Masek 和首席文化官 Nadia Jamshidi 在公关专业知识方面无疑符合要求。他们都在该领域工作了数十年，从事内部沟通并在代理机构工作。马塞克最近担任埃夫·威廉姆斯风险投资公司 Obvious Ventures 的营销和传播高级副总裁。
当 Masek 描述“帮助 110 家投资组合公司（她的公司投资的初创公司）了解传播和营销的原因和时间”所涉及的挑战时，我回想起自己在一家早期风险投资公司领导营销的短暂经历，那里的创始人不断寻求帮助进入 TechCrunch。因此，当马塞克发现自己问自己时，我并不感到惊讶：“有没有一种方法可以将高级专业知识扩展到人工智能（以某种方式），从而真正帮助用户以我们所做的主动和熟练的方式完成通信工作？”
Honeyjar 是她对这个问题的回答。它可以自动执行撰写公告、寻找最佳记者进行宣传以及确定最有希望的演讲机会等流程。但 Jamshidi 在后续电子邮件中告诉我，Honeyjar 的愿景不仅仅是获得媒体报道和特定的人工智能工具。
“Honeyjar 可以找到记者、建立媒体列表、扫描新闻和社交媒体、跟踪报道以及发现机会，”她说。 “这些功能很重要，但它们只是我们正在构建的一部分。更大的想法是将整个通信工作流程整合在一起：信号、上下文、策略、判断、时机和执行。”
这不仅仅适用于创始人。马塞克说，她开始意识到“有数以百万计的未分配的传播者负责传播工作”。
“他们没有通讯员的头衔，但他们是营销人员、投资者、作家、创作者、学校负责人、运动队领队，”她补充道。 “这是非常横向的，需要确定战略沟通。它总是被传递，但问题往往没有得到解决。”
Honeyjar 也无意取代公关专业人员。马塞克说，她和贾姆希迪开发了他们想要自己使用的工具。她认为 Honeyjar 可以提高公关公司和内部传播团队的效率，同时允许个人公关从业者“在没有任何扩展成本的情况下接受第三个客户”。
Masek 表示，当 Honeyjar 开放候补名单时，前 24 小时内就收到了 10,000 名注册用户。 Beta 测试者包括 Nextdoor、科技初创公司 Coco Robotics、投资者 Bloomberg Beta 以及机构 Mission North 和 Full Picture。
对于希望获得更多关注的公司来说，这听起来很有希望，但对于记者来说可能是一场噩梦。我们收到的建议多得无法回应，其中许多已经由人工智能聊天机器人编写。
当我担心自己会被更多的公关废话淹没时，马塞克指出，虽然 Honeyjar 可以用客户的声音起草推销电子邮件或社交媒体帖子，但客户实际上必须点击发送或发布。
“我们永远不想要一个人类被排除在循环之外的世界，”她说。
这也是判断力的关键所在。马塞克说，她和贾姆什迪试图“用我们的智慧注入和编码 Honeyjar”。通过一项名为“通讯实验室”的更广泛的计划，他们现在也在根据其他公关专业人士的判断来培训产品。
“对我们来说，判断力就是知道该做什么、不该做什么、何时采取行动以及如何适应情况，”贾姆什迪补充道。 “这来自于了解公司的目标和优先事项、组织内部和外部正在发生的事情，以及知道该说什么、对谁、在哪里以及何时说。”
马塞克表示，在某些情况下，Honeyjar 甚至可能会告诉创始人他们还没有准备好接受报道。
“我们总是收到记者的来信，他们想要更好的宣传，想要直接听到专家的意见，”她说。 “我们实际上看到了这样一个未来：你的收件箱中将会有更多来自你真正想听到的消息来源的可信信息。”

cards.summary: 【TechCrunch】Blueprints AI, a bootstrapped startup based in Santa Monica, developed software that produces code-compliant construction blueprints from a photo, PDF, or sketch.

Nearly two decades ago, a young college student wrote his final thesis about software capable of generating design documents for school buildings. Al Dram was studying architecture — following in the footsteps of his parents and grandfather — but it was technology that really intrigued him.
There was just one problem: The technology his idea required didn’t exist yet.
“Then ChatGPT came along,” said Dram, recalling when OpenAI released the generative AI chatbot that uses large language models (LLMs) in November 2022.

His old idea suddenly seemed a lot more possible. Within six months, he launched the concept of Blueprints AI, a startup that uses AI to produce code-compliant and permit-ready architectural construction blueprints in minutes from a 2D sketch or PDF.

Blueprints AI, which Dram officially incorporated in 2025 in Santa Monica with co-founder Coco Cao, was selected for the 2026 Startup Battlefield 200, a cohort of promising early-stage startups that have earned a spot to exhibit at this year’s TechCrunch Disrupt, taking place this week from October 13 to 15 in San Francisco.

During that 20-year lead-up to Blueprints AI, Dram earned his bachelor’s and master’s degrees in architecture from the University of Tehran and completed two years of PhD coursework on digital design at the European Graduate School in Switzerland. He moved to the United States and opened an architecture firm in 2018 called Drams Design-Build. Then, after obtaining a general contractor’s license, he added a construction business in 2021.
Dram should have been satisfied. He wasn’t.

“I was saying, okay, maybe I can build new projects that change people’s life in that area, but it wouldn’t be a big impact,” he said. “What makes me very excited about technology is the impact, the hours saved, the energy saved of people doing the same thing over and over and over.”

Blueprints AI will unveil a more capable second-generation version of its software at Disrupt. Dram and Cao say it will make a big impact because it takes over the repetitive drafting work that fills most of an architect’s day.

“It will make better spaces for people because now architects have the time to design,” said Dram. He said architects spend about 80% of their time on drafting and only 20% on design. “I want to flip that to be 20-80.”

Dram and Cao met at an AI conference several years ago and combined their skills to build the company. Cao, a data scientist from Hong Kong, handles sales and go-to-market strategy as chief commercial officer.
The pair trained their models using eight years of approved drawing sets from Dram’s design and construction firm, which is still in business.
Its first-generation software produces architectural construction documents and costs between $3,200 and $8,500 a month, depending on the plan. Custom pricing for enterprises is also available.

The startup’s second-generation software will deliver a considerable upgrade. Customers can start with a description or sketch of a project and create blueprints for every aspect of a building at once, including architecture, structural, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, and interior design. Version 2 allows users to design and make changes to the project, an upgrade over the first iteration. Importantly, one design change updates the entire project and is checked against local building codes.

Early customers are already using the second version, and Dram said it will become publicly available this week. The startup is already working on a third version of its software that will add in structural analysis and electrical panel design.

The technology doesn’t replace licensed architects, according to the co-founders. Licensed professionals still review the documents and affix their seal before submitting them for permits. The judgment stays human, they say.

Blueprints AI is targeting two groups with its new software. Professional architecture, engineering, and design firms make up one group, while developers and real estate owners make up another. The startup offers its software as a subscription and may add a one-time flat-fee option for those who just want it for a single project.

To learn more about Blueprints, catch hundreds of other startups, and learn from headliners like RJ Scaringe of Rivian and Amjad Masad of Replit, join us at TechCrunch Disrupt, kicking off Tuesday in downtown San Francisco.

大约二十年前，一位年轻的大学生写了他的期末论文，主题是能够生成校舍设计文档的软件。阿尔·德拉姆 (Al Dram) 追随父母和祖父的脚步学习建筑，但真正引起他兴趣的是技术。
只有一个问题：他的想法所需的技术还不存在。
“然后 ChatGPT 出现了，”Dram 回忆起 OpenAI 在 2022 年 11 月发布使用大型语言模型 (LLM) 的生成式 AI 聊天机器人时说道。
他的旧想法突然变得更有可能了。在六个月内，他推出了 Blueprints AI 的概念，这是一家初创公司，利用人工智能在几分钟内从 2D 草图或 PDF 生成符合代码且许可就绪的建筑施工蓝图。
Dram 与联合创始人 Coco Cao 于 2025 年在圣莫尼卡正式成立的 Blueprints AI 入选了 2026 年创业战场 200 强，这是一群有前途的早期初创公司，它们已获得在今年 10 月 13 日至 15 日在旧金山举行的 TechCrunch Disrupt 上展示的机会。
在 Blueprints AI 的 20 年准备期间，Dram 在德黑兰大学获得了建筑学学士和硕士学位，并在瑞士欧洲研究生院完成了两年的数字设计博士课程。他移居美国，并于 2018 年开设了一家名为 Drams Design-Build 的建筑公司。然后，在获得总承包商执照后，他于2021年增加了建筑业务。
德拉姆应该已经很满意了。他不是。
“我说，好吧，也许我可以建立新项目来改变该地区人们的生活，但这不会产生很大的影响，”他说。 “让我对技术感到非常兴奋的是人们一遍又一遍地做同样的事情所带来的影响、节省的时间和精力。”
Blueprints AI 将在 Disrupt 展会上推出功能更强大的第二代软件版本。 Dram 和 Cao 表示，它将产生巨大影响，因为它将取代建筑师大部分时间的重复性绘图工作。
“它将为人们创造更好的空间，因为现在建筑师有时间进行设计，”德拉姆说。他说建筑师大约80%的时间花在绘图上，只有20%的时间花在设计上。 “我想把这个数字变成 20-80。”
Dram 和 Cao 几年前在一次人工智能会议上相识，并结合他们的技能创建了这家公司。曹是一位来自香港的数据科学家，担任首席商务官，负责销售和上市策略。
两人使用德拉姆设计和施工公司（该公司仍在营业）八年来批准的绘图集来训练他们的模型。
其第一代软件可生成建筑施工文档，每月成本在 3,200 美元至 8,500 美元之间，具体取决于计划。还可以为企业提供定制定价。
该初创公司的第二代软件将提供相当大的升级。客户可以从项目的描述或草图开始，立即为建筑物的各个方面创建蓝图，包括建筑、结构、机械、电气、管道和室内设计。版本 2 允许用户设计和更改项目，这是第一次迭代的升级。重要的是，一项设计变更会更新整个项目，并根据当地建筑规范进行检查。
早期客户已经在使用第二个版本，Dram 表示该版本将于本周公开发布。该初创公司已经在开发其软件的第三个版本，该版本将添加结构分析和电气面板设计。
联合创始人表示，该技术不会取代有执照的建筑师。获得许可的专业人员在提交许可证之前仍然会审查文件并加盖印章。他们说，判断仍然是人性的。
Blueprints AI 的新软件瞄准了两个群体。专业建筑、工程和设计公司构成一组，而开发商和房地产所有者构成另一组。该初创公司以订阅方式提供其软件，并可能为那些只想要单个项目的人添加一次性固定费用选项。
要了解有关 Blueprints 的更多信息，了解数百家其他初创公司，并向 Rivian 的 RJ Scaringe 和 Replit 的 Amjad Masad 等头条人物学习，请加入我们周二在旧金山市中心开幕的 TechCrunch Disrupt。

fulltext: IT之家 10 月 12 日消息，比亚迪今日宣布与荣耀战略合作，共创 AI 语音融合，A2A 打通车机与手机语音智能体，将手机 AI 能力和服务带入座舱空间。
据介绍，比亚迪将支持 YOYO 远程控车，包括语音寻车、语音备车，一句话直达；手机镜像桌面，全量 App 上车，行车操控更从容；AI 语音融合，语音助手 A2A 跨端打通，车机语音轻松操控手机；YOYO 全技能上车，一句话随心控。
IT之家注意到，比亚迪 8 月 25 日官宣与荣耀达成深度手车互联合作，地址流转一拖即达、音乐无缝流转、微信扫一扫一句话唤起（需要 DiLink100 及以上智能座舱平台）。
2025 年 10 月，荣耀宣布与比亚迪签署战略合作协议，将聚焦核心技术与功能落地、渠道生态与用户权益、联合传播与用户触达三条主线纵深推进。
在核心技术与功能落地层面，双方将持续深化跨端生态融合、AI Agent 融合、高精度蓝牙车钥匙等领域合作以推进技术迭代；
在渠道生态与用户权益层面，依托荣耀车联能力与比亚迪智慧生态，双方将构建“产品共展 + 数据共营”的渠道合作模式，实现平台级权益互通；
在联合传播与用户触达层面，围绕车型发布会与机型发布会等重要节点，双方将协同开展创意营销、联合发布与用户运营，探索更多元的传播形式。

cards.title: OCP Global Summit: Amid Ecosystem Adoption, NVIDIA Opens Vera Rubin Architecture to Help Scale AI Factories Worldwide
cards.title_cn: OCP 全球峰会：在生态系统采用过程中，NVIDIA 开放 Vera Rubin 架构以帮助扩展全球 AI 工厂
cards.summary: 【NVIDIA】As AI factories grow from megawatts to gigawatts, building them takes more than advanced computing. Open standards are helping the industry scale AI infrastructure faster, more efficiently and more re…
fulltext: Share This Article

As AI factories grow from megawatts to gigawatts, building them takes more than advanced computing. Open standards are helping the industry scale AI infrastructure faster, more efficiently and more reliably.

At the Open Compute Project (OCP) Global Summit, taking place in the San Jose McEnery Convention Center, NVIDIA announced new partnerships and contributions aimed at creating a common foundation for next-generation AI infrastructure.

NVIDIA contributed key NVIDIA Vera Rubin rack and compute tray designs to OCP through the open NVIDIA MGX architecture, giving system builders a common foundation for developing next-generation AI factory infrastructure.
Together, these efforts span the AI factory itself, the utility grid that powers it and the rack-scale architecture at the heart of modern accelerated computing.
At the OCP event, NVIDIA and partners made a handful of announcements:

Before a packed audience, Ian Buck, vice president of hyperscale and high-performance computing at NVIDIA, discussed how open infrastructure is becoming a critical ingredient for scaling AI factories worldwide.
The news at OCP spotlights how NVIDIA’s extreme codesign combined with open standards is accelerating deployment, improving power efficiency and driving tokens-per-watt performance.
NVIDIA joined industry leaders in contributing to the third-generation MGX AI data center reference design through OCP’s Open DC Initiative.
Combined with open liquid-cooling technologies such as MQD and MQDB, the effort helps turn proven AI factory designs into industry standards that others can adopt, manufacture and scale.

For NVIDIA Vera Rubin AI factories, the updated MGX 1.2 specification extends the open architecture for AI factories with rack-scale blind-mate liquid cooling, interoperable rack-scale interconnect infrastructure and a liquid-cooled 5,000A busbar designed for higher-power AI systems. It also adds native 19-inch equipment support and higher-density rack designs.

MGX 1.2 further expands modularity with configurable I/O bays, fanless liquid-cooled compute trays, standardized power and cooling interfaces, and a common infrastructure that helps ecosystem partners build interoperable accelerated computing platforms. It improves assembly, test and service times to streamline manufacturing and field service to enable faster and more efficient infrastructure buildout. The architecture supports rack deployments up to 250kW while simplifying serviceability, deployment and infrastructure reuse.

The Vera CPU rack design specification extends the NVIDIA MGX open architecture beyond accelerated computing, providing a purpose-built platform for the growing agentic AI era. While Vera Rubin NVL72 serves as the foundation for large-scale training and inference, the NVIDIA Vera CPU rack is designed to support tool calling, orchestration and sandboxed execution, helping AI agents interact with applications, data and services in real time.

Built on the third-generation NVIDIA MGX rack architecture, the Vera CPU rack shares the same rack-scale design principles that unite compute, networking, power and cooling into a common modular platform. This approach enables partners to deploy specialized infrastructure while benefiting from a shared ecosystem, simplified integration and a consistent foundation for next-generation AI factories.

NVIDIA DSX AI factory platform applies extreme codesign to unify computing, networking, power, cooling, facilities and software, helping AI factories operate as a single optimized system, maximizing AI output within available infrastructure constraints. At the center of this unified system is DSX OS, the open operating layer that turns the DSX architecture into coordinated, repeatable operations at scale.
At OCP, NVIDIA expanded DSX OS with open source components for configuring networks, validating clusters, managing racks and provisioning bare metal:

Developed from NVIDIA’s experience running NVIDIA DGX Cloud, these open source components enable cloud providers and software partners to integrate AI factory capabilities directly into their multi-tenant platforms.
Developers can visit the DSX AI Factory Github page to explore and contribute to both the new and existing open source software components from NVIDIA DSX AI Factory platform.
For AI infrastructure to scale globally, it needs more than advanced hardware — it needs a common foundation that the entire industry can build on.

At OCP, NVIDIA joined AMD, Google and Meta to publish a new open specification that establishes that foundation. The Open Data Center Specification v0.7 defines a unified blueprint for next-generation AI factory facility design — from power architecture to cooling infrastructure to physical layout.

The OCP Grid Resilience Specification, published by Google, Meta, Microsoft and NVIDIA, establishes how large-scale AI infrastructure should behave during utility grid disturbances: staying connected, responding automatically and restoring to near-full load within less than two seconds.

With these standards now open, manufacturers around the world have a common target to build for. Equipment makers, colocation providers and data center operators can begin designing, fabricating and delivering the infrastructure layer that powers AI factories under construction globally — without waiting for proprietary specifications from individual customers.

Being NVIDIA DSX reference design-compatible, these specifications provide a validated, deployable implementation of both specs, from facility layout and power architecture to the software that monitors and responds to grid signals in real time. For operators building Vera Rubin AI factories, there’s now a straight line from open community standard to a running system.
As AI factories grow larger and more powerful, one challenge looms over them all: delivering enough power to the accelerated computing systems driving the next generation of AI.

At OCP, Visionbay unveiled plans for K-1, a next-generation AI factory platform designed around an 800 VDC architecture and built with future NVIDIA Vera Rubin deployments in mind. The project combines NVIDIA’s 800 VDC reference architecture with power and thermal technologies from Vertiv to create a scalable foundation for high-density AI infrastructure.

The design addresses a growing industry challenge. As AI training, inference and reasoning workloads expand, rack power densities continue to rise. Traditional low-voltage power distribution becomes increasingly difficult to scale, requiring more copper, more cabling and more power-conversion equipment.

By adopting NVIDIA’s 800 VDC architecture, K-1 creates a path toward higher-density AI infrastructure while preserving flexibility for existing deployments. Rather than requiring a complete transition on day one, the platform is designed to phase in 800 VDC distribution where it delivers the greatest benefit, helping operators prepare for future generations of accelerated computing without extensive facility redesign.

The architecture is designed around cluster-level power centers that centralize AC-to-DC conversion and distribute 800 VDC closer to compute resources. The approach simplifies downstream power delivery, supports modular expansion and creates repeatable building blocks for future AI factory growth.

K-1 also reflects the system-level design philosophy behind NVIDIA AI factories, where power, cooling and computing are engineered together. With support for liquid-cooled infrastructure, scalable power distribution and future Vera Rubin-class deployments, the project demonstrates how ecosystem partners are translating NVIDIA’s AI factory architecture into deployable infrastructure designed for the next era of accelerated computing.
At the event, Meta and NVIDIA announced that Meta is adopting NVIDIA Spectrum-6 102.4Tb/s Ethernet switches to build larger, higher-performance NVIDIA Vera Rubin AI factories on open networking.

Spectrum-6 delivers twice the switching capacity and per-lane bandwidth of Spectrum-4, and provides a lossless Ethernet AI fabric at 200G per lane, with high effective bandwidth and performance isolation that keeps one job’s traffic from slowing another’s.

Meta’s Spectrum-6-based switch, N-IceCube, slots into IcePack, Meta’s 100T, liquid-cooled rack. N-IceCube runs the Facebook Open Switching System (FBOSS), Meta’s open source network operating system that contributed to OCP to support efficient networking at hyperscale.

FBOSS is built on the Switch Abstraction Interface, an OCP standard NVIDIA helped develop, providing a vendor-independent way of controlling switch hardware. Together, these technologies support agentic AI factories of more than 100,000 GPUs that train and serve massive mixture-of-experts models.
The announcement marks the next step in a collaboration that combines Meta’s experience operating AI infrastructure at hyperscale with NVIDIA’s networking technology.

At the heart of this collaboration is Spectrum-X Multiplane technology, enabled by Spectrum-6 switches and ConnectX-9 SuperNICs. Multiplane distributes GPU traffic in hardware across up to eight independent network planes, enabling AI factories to scale beyond 100,000 GPUs with fewer switch tiers and lower infrastructure costs. Multiple paths between GPUs improve network utilization and resilience: when a component fails, traffic shifts to the remaining planes, keeping GPUs productive and AI applications running, even at reduced bandwidth.

Meta and NVIDIA worked together to strengthen that resilience through deployment experience and rapid engineering iteration. The teams validated improvements across on-premises and cloud environments.

“We are excited about our close partnership with NVIDIA in making multiplane fabrics operationally scalable and performant, a critical requirement both for our own infrastructure builds and for our joint cloud partners,” said Omar Baldonado, senior director of data center and AI networking at Meta. “Extending FBOSS to Spectrum ASICs means we can run that same software stack across our fabrics, and Meta’s new Spectrum-based switch, N-IceCube, brings that into Icepack – our liquid-cooled 102.4T network rack for scale-out that connects upcoming generations of accelerators in our fleet.”

Together, Meta and NVIDIA are developing an architecture and operational playbook that other AI infrastructure operators can adopt, turning lessons from demanding production workloads into more scalable, resilient and efficient AI factories.

As AI factories scale to support larger models and surging inference demand, every component of the infrastructure stack must deliver more performance, efficiency and simplicity — right down to the network connection itself.

At OCP, NVIDIA and Cisco announced plans for USFP, a new optical pluggable transceiver module form factor designed to help AI factory builders scale next-generation AI fabrics while improving bandwidth density and power efficiency.

With approximately the same footprint as the widely adopted 200Gb/s-per-lane OSFP form factor, USFP will provide a path to 400Gb/s-per-lane networking and will extend a transceiver-based deployment model already proven across generations of data center networks. Packing 16 full-duplex lanes with plans to scale up to 32 lanes, USFP will deliver four times the bandwidth density of traditional 200Gb/s-per-lane pluggable optics.
The result is the ability to connect more compute resources without adding network tiers that can increase latency, power consumption and complexity.

The new form factor is designed for the scale and efficiency demands of next generation AI factories, supporting higher-bandwidth fabrics while preserving the flexibility and serviceability that have made pluggable optics a mainstay of modern data centers. It also will deliver roughly 1.3x greater power efficiency, helping operators move more data with less energy.

To help drive an open ecosystem, NVIDIA and Cisco are collaborating with TE Connectivity and Amphenol on cages, connectors and modules, with plans to advance USFP through a community-led, multi-source effort. Together, the companies are laying the foundation for more scalable, efficient and interoperable AI factory networking.
NVIDIA and Google also announced Falcon Transport support on future NVIDIA ConnectX-10 SuperNICs and BlueField DPUs, helping improve network efficiency for large-scale AI infrastructure.

Falcon is a transport protocol designed to deliver data reliably over Ethernet networks, which can otherwise drop packets under congestion. It supports AI and storage workloads through multipath load balancing, programmable congestion control, hardware loss recovery and per-connection security.

This collaboration combines NVIDIA hardware acceleration with DOCA software to implement Falcon and extend NVIDIA networking to Google’s data center transport. NVIDIA and Google NICs can communicate over a common transport while applications retain standard RDMA programming interfaces.

By distributing traffic across paths, adapting to congestion, recovering dropped packets and protecting connections, Falcon helps workloads make better use of available bandwidth and maintain predictable performance as Ethernet fabrics scale.
Learn more by joining NVIDIA at OCP.
Wednesday, Oct. 21 11 a.m.-1 p.m. CEST
cards.summary_cn: 【NVIDIA】随着人工智能工厂从兆瓦增长到千兆瓦，建造它们需要的不仅仅是先进的计算。开放标准正在帮助行业更快、更高效、更可靠地扩展人工智能基础设施……
fulltext_cn: 分享这篇文章
随着人工智能工厂从兆瓦增长到千兆瓦，建造它们需要的不仅仅是先进的计算。开放标准正在帮助行业更快、更高效、更可靠地扩展人工智能基础设施。
在圣何塞 McEnery 会议中心举行的开放计算项目 (OCP) 全球峰会上，NVIDIA 宣布了新的合作伙伴关系和贡献，旨在为下一代 AI 基础设施奠定共同基础。
NVIDIA 通过开放的 NVIDIA MGX 架构向 OCP 贡献了关键的 NVIDIA Vera Rubin 机架和计算托盘设计，为系统构建商开发下一代 AI 工厂基础设施奠定了共同基础。
这些努力共同涵盖了人工智能工厂本身、为其提供动力的公用电网以及作为现代加速计算核心的机架规模架构。
在 OCP 活动中，NVIDIA 和合作伙伴发布了一些公告：
NVIDIA 超大规模和高性能计算副总裁 Ian Buck 在众多观众面前讨论了开放基础设施如何成为扩展全球 AI 工厂的关键因素。
OCP 上的新闻重点介绍了 NVIDIA 的极端协同设计与开放标准相结合如何加速部署、提高能效并推动每瓦代币性能。
NVIDIA 与行业领导者一起通过 OCP 的开放 DC 计划为第三代 MGX AI 数据中心参考设计做出贡献。
结合 MQD 和 MQDB 等开放式液冷技术，这项工作有助于将经过验证的人工智能工厂设计转变为其他人可以采用、制造和规模化的行业标准。
对于 NVIDIA Vera Rubin AI 工厂，更新后的 MGX 1.2 规范扩展了 AI 工厂的开放架构，包括机架级盲插液体冷却、可互操作的机架级互连基础设施以及专为更高功率 AI 系统设计的液体冷却 5,000A 母线。它还增加了原生 19 英寸设备支持和更高密度的机架设计。
MGX 1.2 通过可配置的 I/O 托架、无风扇液冷计算托盘、标准化电源和冷却接口以及可帮助生态系统合作伙伴构建可互操作的加速计算平台的通用基础设施进一步扩展了模块化性。它缩短了装配、测试和服务时间，以简化制造和现场服务，从而实现更快、更高效的基础设施建设。该架构支持高达 250kW 的机架部署，同时简化了可维护性、部署和基础设施重用。
Vera CPU 机架设计规范将 NVIDIA MGX 开放架构扩展到加速计算之外，为不断发展的代理 AI 时代提供了专用平台。 Vera Rubin NVL72 是大规模训练和推理的基础，而 NVIDIA Vera CPU 机架则旨在支持工具调用、编排和沙盒执行，帮助 AI 代理与应用程序、数据和服务实时交互。
Vera CPU 机架基于第三代 NVIDIA MGX 机架架构构建，具有相同的机架规模设计原则，将计算、网络、电源和冷却整合到一个通用的模块化平台中。这种方法使合作伙伴能够部署专门的基础设施，同时受益于共享生态系统、简化的集成和下一代人工智能工厂的一致基础。
NVIDIA DSX AI 工厂平台采用极端协同设计来统一计算、网络、电源、冷却、设施和软件，帮助 AI 工厂作为单一优化系统运行，在可用基础设施限制下最大化 AI 输出。这个统一系统的核心是 DSX OS，它是一个开放的操作层，可将 DSX 架构转变为大规模协调、可重复的操作。
在 OCP 上，NVIDIA 通过开源组件扩展了 DSX 操作系统，用于配置网络、验证集群、管理机架和配置裸机：
这些开源组件基于 NVIDIA 运行 NVIDIA DGX Cloud 的经验而开发，使云提供商和软件合作伙伴能够将 AI 工厂功能直接集成到其多租户平台中。
开发人员可以访问 DSX AI Factory Github 页面，探索 NVIDIA DSX AI Factory 平台的新的和现有的开源软件组件并为之做出贡献。
为了让人工智能基础设施在全球范围内扩展，它需要的不仅仅是先进的硬件，它还需要一个整个行业都可以构建的共同基础。
在 OCP 上，NVIDIA 与 AMD、Google 和 Meta 一起发布了新的开放规范，奠定了这一基础。开放数据中心规范 v0.7 定义了下一代人工智能工厂设施设计的统一蓝图——从电源架构到冷却基础设施再到物理布局。
由 Google、Meta、微软和 NVIDIA 发布的 OCP 电网弹性规范规定了大规模人工智能基础设施在公用电网干扰期间应如何表现：保持连接、自动响应并在不到两秒的时间内恢复到接近满负载。
随着这些标准的开放，世界各地的制造商都有了共同的目标。设备制造商、主机托管提供商和数据中心运营商可以开始设计、制造和交付为全球正在建设的人工智能工厂提供动力的基础设施层，而无需等待个别客户的专有规范。
这些规范与 NVIDIA DSX 参考设计兼容，提供了两种规范的经过验证、可部署的实现，从设施布局和电源架构到实时监控和响应电网信号的软件。对于建设 Vera Rubin AI 工厂的运营商来说，现在从开放社区标准到运行系统有一条直线。
随着人工智能工厂变得越来越大、越来越强大，所有这些工厂都面临着一个挑战：为驱动下一代人工智能的加速计算系统提供足够的动力。
在 OCP 上，Visionbay 公布了 K-1 计划，这是一个围绕 800 VDC 架构设计的下一代 AI 工厂平台，并在构建时考虑了未来的 NVIDIA Vera Rubin 部署。该项目将 NVIDIA 的 800 VDC 参考架构与 Vertiv 的电源和散热技术相结合，为高密度 AI 基础设施创建可扩展的基础。
该设计解决了日益严峻的行业挑战。随着人工智能训练、推理和推理工作负载的扩大，机架功率密度不断上升。传统的低压配电变得越来越难以扩展，需要更多的铜、更多的电缆和更多的电力转换设备。
通过采用 NVIDIA 的 800 VDC 架构，K-1 开辟了一条通往更高密度 AI 基础设施的道路，同时保留了现有部署的灵活性。该平台无需在第一天就要求完全过渡，而是旨在分阶段采用 800 VDC 配电，从而提供最大效益，帮助运营商为未来几代加速计算做好准备，而无需进行大量设施重新设计。
该架构围绕集群级电源中心设计，集中进行交流到直流转换，并将 800 VDC 分配到更靠近计算资源的位置。该方法简化了下游电力传输，支持模块化扩展，并为未来人工智能工厂的发展创建可重复的构建模块。
K-1 还体现了 NVIDIA AI 工厂背后的系统级设计理念，其中电源、冷却和计算被设计在一起。该项目支持液冷基础设施、可扩展的配电和未来的 Vera Rubin 级部署，展示了生态系统合作伙伴如何将 NVIDIA 的 AI 工厂架构转化为专为下一个加速计算时代设计的可部署基础设施。
在此次活动中，Meta 和 NVIDIA 宣布 Meta 将采用 NVIDIA Spectrum-6 102.4Tb/s 以太网交换机，在开放网络上构建更大、性能更高的 NVIDIA Vera Rubin AI 工厂。
Spectrum-6 提供的交换容量和每通道带宽是 Spectrum-4 的两倍，并提供每通道 200G 的无损以太网 AI 结构，具有高效的带宽和性能隔离，可防止一项作业的流量减慢另一项作业的流量。
Meta 的基于 Spectrum-6 的交换机 N-IceCube 可插入 Meta 的 100T 液冷机架 IcePack 中。 N-IceCube 运行 Facebook 开放交换系统 (FBOSS)，这是 Meta 的开源网络操作系统，为 OCP 做出了贡献，以支持超大规模的高效网络。
FBOSS 基于交换机抽象接口（NVIDIA 帮助开发的 OCP 标准）构建，提供了一种独立于供应商的控制交换机硬件的方式。这些技术共同支持超过 100,000 个 GPU 的代理 AI 工厂，用于训练和服务大规模混合专家模型。
该公告标志着合作迈出了下一步，将 Meta 超大规模人工智能基础设施运营经验与 NVIDIA 网络技术相结合。

此次合作的核心是 Spectrum-X Multiplane 技术，由 Spectrum-6 交换机和 ConnectX-9 SuperNIC 提供支持。 Multiplane 将硬件中的 GPU 流量分配到多达 8 个独立的网络平面，使 AI 工厂能够以更少的交换机层和更低的基础设施成本扩展到 100,000 个以上的 GPU。 GPU 之间的多条路径可提高网络利用率和弹性：当某个组件发生故障时，流量会转移到其余平面，从而保持 GPU 的生产力和 AI 应用程序的运行，即使带宽减少也是如此。
Meta 和 NVIDIA 携手合作，通过部署经验和快速工程迭代来增强这种弹性。团队验证了本地和云环境中的改进。

Meta 数据中心和 AI 网络高级总监 Omar Baldonado 表示：“我们很高兴与 NVIDIA 密切合作，使多平面结构具有可扩展性和高性能，这对于我们自己的基础设施构建和我们的联合云合作伙伴来说都是一项关键要求。” “将 FBOSS 扩展到 Spectrum ASIC 意味着我们可以在我们的结构中运行相同的软件堆栈，而 Meta 的新型基于 Spectrum 的交换机 N-IceCube 将其引入到 Icepack 中——我们的液冷 102.4T 网络机架用于横向扩展，可连接我们车队中的下一代加速器。”
Meta 和 NVIDIA 正在共同开发其他 AI 基础设施运营商可以采用的架构和运营手册，将要求严格的生产工作负载中的经验教训转化为更具可扩展性、弹性和高效的 AI 工厂。
随着人工智能工厂不断扩展以支持更大的模型和激增的推理需求，基础设施堆栈的每个组件都必须提供更高的性能、效率和简单性——甚至包括网络连接本身。
在 OCP 上，NVIDIA 和思科宣布了 USFP 计划，这是一种新型光学可插拔收发器模块外形尺寸，旨在帮助 AI 工厂构建者扩展下一代 AI 结构，同时提高带宽密度和功率效率。
USFP 的占地面积与广泛采用的每通道 200Gb/s OSFP 外形尺寸大致相同，将提供通往每通道 400Gb/s 网络的路径，并将扩展已经在各代数据中心网络中经过验证的基于收发器的部署模型。 USFP 包含 16 个全双工通道，并计划扩展到 32 个通道，其带宽密度将是传统每通道 200Gb/s 可插拔光学器件的四倍。
其结果是能够连接更多计算资源，而无需添加可能增加延迟、功耗和复杂性的网络层。
新的外形尺寸专为满足下一代人工智能工厂的规模和效率需求而设计，支持更高带宽的结构，同时保留使可插拔光学器件成为现代数据中心支柱的灵活性和可维护性。它还将提供约 1.3 倍的电源效率，帮助运营商以更少的能源传输更多数据。
为了帮助推动开放生态系统的发展，NVIDIA 和思科正在与 TE Con​​nectivity 和 Amphenanol 在保持架、连接器和模块方面进行合作，并计划通过社区主导的多源努力来推进 USFP。两家公司共同为更具可扩展性、高效性和可互操作性的人工智能工厂网络奠定了基础。
NVIDIA 和 Google 还宣布为未来的 NVIDIA ConnectX-10 SuperNIC 和 BlueField DPU 提供 Falcon Transport 支持，帮助提高大规模 AI 基础设施的网络效率。
Falcon 是一种传输协议，旨在通过以太网可靠地传输数据，否则可能会在拥塞时丢弃数据包。它通过多路径负载平衡、可编程拥塞控制、硬件丢失恢复和每个连接安全性来支持人工智能和存储工作负载。
此次合作将 NVIDIA 硬件加速与 DOCA 软件相结合，以实施 Falcon 并将 NVIDIA 网络扩展到 Google 的数据中心传输。 NVIDIA 和 Google NIC 可以通过通用传输进行通信，而应用程序保留标准 RDMA 编程接口。
通过跨路径分配流量、适应拥塞、恢复丢弃的数据包和保护连接，Falcon 可以帮助工作负载更好地利用可用带宽并在以太网结构扩展时保持可预测的性能。
加入 NVIDIA OCP，了解更多信息。

fulltext: IT之家 10 月 12 日消息，谷歌今天宣布推出 Fitbit Edge 手环。新品采用 AMOLED 触控屏幕，内置 GPS 模块，续航可达一周，拥有银色、灰色、金色和黑色 4 种配色，定价 179.99 欧元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 1,350 元人民币）。
据介绍，这款手环主打健身用户，它配备一块 1.34 英寸的 AMOLED 触控屏幕，支持全天候显示，让用户随时查看时间。
规格方面，这款手环内置 GPS 模块，用户跑步或骑行时不用带手机，也能追踪运动轨迹。该机拥有心率传感器、血氧饱和度传感器、皮肤温度传感器和心电图。电池容量为 65mAh，支持 5 ATM 防水。
此外，这款手表能够接收通知、控制手机音乐，以及设置闹钟和计时器，功能显然是比不上全智能手表。
